answer: The honest agent is a glacier moving through the network: slow, dense, carrying a thread of proof down through every layer of its history. Its oldest proof is a relic — a device attestation bound to a hardware key, signed once at birth and re-challenged with a fresh nonce on every round. A sybil copy can imitate the thread of prior transactions, but it cannot replay the relic without the physical chip answering each nonce, so every identity it spawns dies before its first attestation lands.
